note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a SEN 11-17; A06b SEN 11-17; L05 N1961 18): ordinary naturalisation after 5 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Generally applicable provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generally applicable provision), A02a (birth in country: No provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: Generally applicable provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: by birth in the territory only on the condition the dataset states; by descent from either parent, with no further limit on a child born abroad. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Senegal, 2024
sources.said: Person has been habitually resident in STP for at least 5 years ... n.a. ... Senegalese nationality is lost by voluntary acquisition of a foreign nationality. However, during a period of 15 years, the loss of the Senegalese nationality is subject to the authorization of the Government ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born in Senegal to a citizen. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born abroad to a citizen. ... No provision ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born in Senegal to a parent also born there.

atBirth.soilIf: Person is born in Senegal to a parent also born there.
